entries.name: CocoaPods
entries.definition: A dependency manager for Swift and Objective-C projects that downloads and links third-party libraries.

entries.name: CocoonJS
entries.definition: A tool from Ludei that packages HTML5 and JavaScript apps and games as native mobile apps with accelerated canvas rendering.

entries.name: Cognitive computing
entries.definition: Computing systems that imitate aspects of human thinking, such as learning, reasoning and understanding language, using methods like machine learning and natural language processing.

entries.name: Cognitive load
entries.definition: The amount of mental effort being used in working memory at a given time, a concept used in teaching and interface design to avoid overloading people.

entries.name: Collaboration
entries.definition: Working jointly with others, sharing information and effort, to reach a shared goal.

entries.name: Collaboration software
entries.definition: Software that lets groups work together on shared tasks and documents, for example through shared files, chat and project boards.

entries.name: Collaborative Planning, Forecasting and Replenishment
entries.definition: A supply-chain practice in which trading partners jointly plan, forecast and replenish stock using shared data.

entries.name: Color matching
entries.definition: Choosing or adjusting colours so that a product or print matches a reference colour, as in paint, printing, textiles and cosmetics.

entries.name: Color, material and finish design
entries.definition: Choosing and specifying the colours, materials and surface finishes of a product as part of industrial design.

entries.name: Color rendering index
entries.definition: A scale up to 100 that rates how faithfully a light source shows the colours of objects compared with a reference light.

entries.name: Combine harvester
entries.definition: A farm machine that cuts, threshes and cleans grain crops in a single pass.

entries.name: Commercial loan documentation
entries.definition: Preparing and reviewing the agreements and security documents that set out the terms of a commercial loan.

entries.name: Commercial off-the-shelf
entries.definition: Ready-made hardware or software products bought from a supplier and used as they are, rather than built specially for the buyer.

entries.name: Commissioning, qualification and validation
entries.definition: Engineering activities, common in pharmaceutical manufacturing, that verify and document that facilities, equipment and systems are installed correctly and perform as intended.

entries.name: Common Criteria
entries.definition: The international standard, ISO/IEC 15408, for evaluating the security of IT products.

entries.name: Common Language Specification
entries.definition: A set of rules in Microsoft's .NET Framework that languages must follow so that code written in one .NET language can be used from another.

entries.name: CommonJS
entries.definition: A specification for JavaScript modules and other server-side interfaces, best known for the require and module.exports module format used by Node.js.

entries.name: Commons-based peer production
entries.definition: A way of producing goods in which many people collaborate voluntarily without central ownership or markets, as in open-source software and Wikipedia.

entries.name: Communication
entries.definition: Conveying information and ideas clearly to others through speaking, writing and listening.

entries.name: Communication software
entries.definition: Software for exchanging messages and conversations between people, such as email, chat, voice calls and video conferencing.

entries.name: Communication theories
entries.definition: Theories that explain how people and groups create, send and interpret messages.

entries.name: Community advocacy
entries.definition: Speaking up for a community's needs and rights and helping its members influence the decisions that affect them.

entries.name: Community nutrition
entries.definition: The part of nutrition concerned with improving the diet and health of groups and populations through education, programmes and policy.

entries.name: Community resilience
entries.definition: The capacity of a community to prepare for, withstand and recover from disasters and other disruptions.

entries.name: Compiler development
entries.definition: Designing and building compilers, the programs that translate source code into machine code or another language.

entries.name: Complaint investigation
entries.definition: Looking into complaints from customers, employees or the public to establish the facts and decide how to resolve them.

entries.name: Compliance risk management
entries.definition: Identifying, assessing and controlling the risk that an organisation breaks laws, regulations or its own policies.

entries.name: Compliance testing
entries.definition: Checking whether processes, controls or products meet the laws, regulations or standards that apply to them.

entries.name: ComponentOne
entries.definition: A commercial suite of user-interface controls and data components for .NET and web applications.

entries.name: Composite pattern
entries.definition: A structural software design pattern that lets single objects and groups of objects be treated the same way through a shared tree-shaped interface.

entries.name: Computational design
entries.definition: Using algorithms and code to generate, analyse and refine designs, as in parametric architecture and product design.

entries.name: Computer architecture
entries.definition: The design and organisation of a computer's components, such as the processor, memory and instruction set.

entries.name: Computer-assisted audit tools and techniques (CAATTs)
entries.definition: The use of software tools and techniques to analyse data and automate audit procedures.
variants: Computer Assisted Audit Tools And Techniques (CAATT)

entries.name: Computer-assisted qualitative data analysis software (CAQDAS)
entries.definition: Software for organising, coding and analysing non-numerical data such as interviews, text and recordings.

entries.name: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act
entries.definition: A US federal law that prohibits unauthorised access to protected computers and related computer crimes.

entries.name: Computer networking
entries.definition: Understanding communication and interconnection of computing systems.

entries.name: Computer science
entries.definition: The study of computation, algorithms, data and the design of computer systems and software.

entries.name: Computerized system validation
entries.definition: The documented process of showing that a computerised system consistently does what it is meant to do, used in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals.

entries.name: ComputerRx
entries.definition: A pharmacy management software product used to handle prescriptions and pharmacy operations.

entries.name: Concision
entries.definition: Expressing ideas clearly in no more words than are needed.
